editorial_reason: A sigma-algebra on X is a family of subsets of the powerset P(X), so the ordinary non-strict subset relation is a prerequisite. The separate axioms requiring complements and countable unions are additional, not supplied by the subset definition.

A nonnegative measure is a countably additive set function defined on a sigma-algebra of measurable subsets. The sigma-algebra's complement and union closure is a precise prerequisite, without assuming topology or finite mass.

The source measure definition explicitly specifies an extended-nonnegative-valued function from the measurable sets in Σ, so total single-valued assignment is a foundational prerequisite. Countable additivity and μ(∅)=0 are extra axioms.

A raw moment of a nonnegative Borel or Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure requires a countably additive nonnegative set function on a sigma-algebra. The independently screened generic measure supplies that object, while Borel structure, measurability and integration remain missing concepts.

The nth raw moment uses the power function assigning each real x its nth power. The screened mapping-as-total-single-valued-assignment supplies the underlying functional object; μ-integrability is an additional property.

The DLMF orthogonality formulation presupposes a nonnegative Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure, which is a special nonnegative countably additive measure. The source's extra support, bounded-function and finite-moment conditions are not implied by the general measure definition.
